The last stage in the tactics phase is to write down or record, your list of reassessment triggers a Trader who clearly lays out. Her plan is way ahead of most Traders. Reassessment triggers are important because once you have a trade on, you'll be influenced by all sorts of new information that is mostly noise numbers jiggle on a screen, random headline, scroll by your heart rate ticks up. For example, any day trade can have a reassessment or firm exit time of 4 p.m. when the main New York Stock Exchange trading session ends. Many good trades. Have a Time trigger. Another example, say, you've done a ton of work on today's US, retail sales number and you expect it will be weak. You go long bonds at 7:45 a.m. in anticipation of the release at 8:30 a.m. You believe that most of the new information from economic data gets fully priced within 10 minutes. Does it make any sense to keep the trade past 8:45 or maybe 9:00 a.m. at the latest? Probably not. So you put a reassessment trigger at 8:45 a.m. 2 level at which, to tighten the stop loss. Note that I'm using the term reassessment triggers, but often these are action triggers. The last example, is an action trigger. I use reassessment trigger and action trigger interchangeably.
